about: Decision 0064 step 3 and decision 0107 (EA-0124): lakes as of 1318 that people drained later, and water made later that was dry land in 1318, as works areas (tools/bake_lakes_1318.py -> earthdata/works-1318-4.bin, works rules 6). level: the water's level in metres (EGM2008, as GLO-90). outline: 'ohm' (OpenHistoricalMap, CC0) or 'osm' (OpenStreetMap, ODbL) element, kept in tools/lakes-1318/<key>.geojson by tools/fetch_lakes_1318.py; or 'fill': GLO-90 (Copernicus DEM, rawdata/copernicus-glo90) below 'below' metres, connected to 'seed' [lat, lon] within 'box' [lon0, lat0, lon1, lat1], contoured at that height; 'grow_m' widens the area. Sources and the reasoning for each level: the research note docs/research/lakes-1318-2026-11/research-drained-lakes.md.

areas.name: Aral Sea of 1318 (the Kerderi low stand)
areas.cite: Krivonogov et al. 2014, Gondwana Research 26: about 29 m (27-30) in the 12th-15th centuries; western basin full, a shallow lagoon in the eastern basin

areas.name: Lake Texcoco
areas.cite: OpenHistoricalMap 'Lago de Texcoco' (to 1635), CC0; level about 2,236-2,240 m; the islands west of 99.10 W (Tenochtitlan, Tlatelolco and their chinampas, from 1325) are lake in 1318, the Peñón hills stay islands

areas.name: Lake Zumpango
areas.cite: OpenHistoricalMap 'Lago de Zumpango' (to 1700), CC0; drawn at Xaltocan's level (2,241 m), where they meet (it stood a few metres higher: a block at 1:10)

areas.name: Lake Fucino
areas.cite: Giraudi 1989/1990: the shore before the Torlonia drainage (1855-1878) at about 660 m; 140-155 km² (OpenHistoricalMap 'Lago Fucino', CC0: 141 km²)

areas.name: Lake Copais
areas.cite: Mamassis et al. (after Constantinidis 1984): water 92-97 m, spilling to the eastern sinkholes above 97 m; drained land 241 km²

areas.name: Whittlesey Mere
areas.cite: OpenStreetMap 'Whittlesey Mere' (historic=yes), ODbL; about +1 m OD before the fen shrank

areas.name: Ogura-ike
areas.cite: OpenHistoricalMap '巨椋池' (to 1933), CC0: the lake as drained in 1933-41, smaller than in 1318

areas.name: Lake Karla (Boebeis)
areas.cite: 50.10 m in 1921 on ground that has sunk since (cracks from pumping); 45-180 km² by season and year, drawn at about 130 km² (GLO-90 below 48 m); drained 1962

areas.name: Lake Amik (Lake of Antioch)
areas.cite: 79.4 m in 1949, 83.4 m in 1953 (DSİ), on peat burned down 1-1.5 m since; 90-100 km² of lake, 310 with its marsh: drawn at about 150 km² (GLO-90 below 79 m); drained 1954-1975

areas.name: Hachirōgata
areas.cite: a brackish lagoon of about 220 km² at sea level, reclaimed 1957-1977

areas.name: Salton Sea (dry in 1318)
areas.cite: made by the Colorado River's breach of 1905-1907; Lake Cahuilla stood high before 1241 and in 1459-1503 only (Rockwell et al. 2022)
